To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
daily autonomous and controlled goal motivation predict academic emotions, applying to both within-person processes and individual differences.
students' autonomous and controlled educational goal motivation are important determinants of academic emotions, and that these associations are both intra- and inter-personal.
daily autonomous goals predict positive emotions, whereas daily controlled goals predict negative emotions, and both kinds of goal motivation predict determination in students’ academic lives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether and how students' goal motivation predicts their emotions in everyday academic life.
the question of how students' goal motivation relates to academic emotion states.
the role of daily autonomous educational goals in students’ positive academic emotion states, and with daily controlled educational goals in negative academic emotion states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the more students’ goals are self-determined and autonomous, the higher their positive emotions, and the lower their negative emotions in everyday situations, and that these processes are similar in the within- and between-person levels.
autonomous motivation is associated with positive emotions and determination, and controlled motivation with negative emotions and lack of determination.
autonomous educational goals are associated with positive emotions and determination, whereas controlled motivation predicts negative emotions and determination.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
students who set autonomous goals for the upcoming day experience more positive emotions and less negative emotions than students who do not set autonomous goals.
the more students’ goals were self-determined, the higher was their positive emotionality, whereas controlled goals were associated with negative emotions.
students' goal motivation is an antecedent of academic emotions in the context of SDT.
The main takeaway from our work is that
students' daily goal motivation can be used to understand their academic emotions.

the SDT framework can be applied to the real-time analysis of students’ daily lives, and that it is possible to identify the role of autonomous and controlled motivation in students’ daily academic emotions.
students’ goal motivation is a relevant antecedent of their academic emotions.
